questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The platelets are drifting with the blood flowing in a streamline flow through a horizontal artery as shown below:

Artery is contracted in region $II$. Choose the correct statement.
options: As the platelets enter a constriction, the platelets gets squeezed closer together in the narrow region and hence the fluid pressure must rise there.
As the platelets enter a constriction, pressure is lower there.
The artery's cross section area is smaller in the constriction and thus the pressure must be larger there because pressure equals the force divided by area
Pressure is same in all the parts of the artery
questions.solution:
Using equation of continuity

${A}_{1}{V}_{1} = {A}_{2}{V}_{2}$

where ${A}_{1} \text{ and } {A}_{2}$ are cross-section area of region $I $ region-$II$.

as ${A}_{2} < {A}_{1}$

$⇒ {V}_{2} > {V}_{1}$

Using Bernouilli's equation

$P + \dfrac{1}{2}ρV^{2} =$ constant

as ${V}_{2} > {V}_{1}$

${P}_{2} < {P}_{1}$

therefore pressure will be lower at constriction.

Fraction of thickness of ice block out of water is

So, minimum length of rope required $\approx$ thickness of ice $\times 0. 1 = 8 \times 0. 1 = 0. 8m$
Hence, nearest option is $0. 9m$.

questions.q:
Consider the configuration of a stationary water tank of cross-section area ${A}_{0}$ and a small bucket as shown in figure below;

What should be the speed $v$ of the bucket, so that the water leaking out of a hole of cross-section area $A$ (as shown) from the water tank does not fall outside the bucket?

(Take, $h = 5m, H = 5m, g = 10m / s^{2}, A = 5{cm}^{2}$ and ${A}_{0} = 500{cm}^{2}$).
questions.solution:
Velocity of outflow (efflux) from hole $= \sqrt{2gh}$.

Range of water jet,

$x = \sqrt{2gh}\times$ Time of fall

$= \sqrt{2gh} \times \sqrt{\dfrac{2H}{g}} = 2\sqrt{hH}$

Velocity $v$ of bucket is

$v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}2\sqrt{hH}$

$= 2\sqrt{H}. \dfrac{d\sqrt{h}}{dt}$

$⇒ v = 2\sqrt{H}. \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{h}}. \dfrac{dh}{dt}$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{H}{h}}. \dfrac{dh}{dt}... ( i )$

Now, using equation of continuity at area ${A}_{0}$ and area A$, we have

A{v}_{1} = {A}_{0}V$

where, ${v}_{1} = \sqrt{2gh}$

and $V = \dfrac{dh}{dt}$.

$∴ A\sqrt{2gh} = {A}_{0} \left(\dfrac{dh}{dt}\right)

Substituting for \dfrac{dh}{dt} from Eq $( i )$, we get

$v = $\sqrt{\dfrac{H}{h}}$. $\dfrac{A}{A0}$. $\sqrt{2gh}$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{5}}. \left(\dfrac{5}{500}\right). \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 5}

$= $\dfrac{1}{10}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$

$= 0. 1\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider the wall of a dam to be straight with height $H$ and length $L$. It holds a lake of water of height $h  \left(h < H\right)$ on one side. Let the density of water be ${ρ}_{w}$ Denote the torque about the axis along the bottom length of the wall by ${τ}_{1}$. Denote also a similar torque due to the water up to height $h / 2$ and wall length $L / 2$ by ${τ}_{2}$. Then, ${τ}_{1} / {τ}_{2} (ignore atmospheric pressure) is$
questions.solution:
Consider a strip of width $dy$ at a depth $\left(h - y\right)$ below the surface. 

Torque on bottom length ( $OZ$ in diagram) due to force of water on strip of width $dy$ is 

$dτ =$ Force $\times$ Perpendicular distance $=$ Pressure $\times$ Area $\times$ Distance

$dτ = ρg\left(h - y\right) \cdot \left(L \cdot dy\right) \cdot y$

So, torque on bottom length due to complete volume of water, 

${τ}_{1} = {∫}_{0}^{h}Lρg\left(h - y\right)y \cdot dy$

$= Lρg\left[{∫}_{0}^{h}\left(hy - {y}^{2}\right)dy\right]$

$= Lρg{\left[\dfrac{h{y}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{{y}^{3}}{3}\right]}_{0}^{h}$

$= Lρg\left[\dfrac{{h}^{3}}{2} - \dfrac{{h}^{3}}{3}\right]$

or ${τ}_{1} = \dfrac{Lρg{h}^{3}}{6} . . . ( i )$

and torque due to water upto height $\dfrac{h}{2}$ and wall length $\dfrac{1}{2}$, ${τ}_{2} = {∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{h}{2}}\dfrac{L}{2}ρg\left(\dfrac{h}{2} - y\right)ydy$

$= \dfrac{L}{2}ρg{\left[\left(\dfrac{h{y}^{2}}{4} - \dfrac{h{y}^{3}}{3}\right)\right]}_{0}^{h}$

$= \dfrac{L}{2}ρg\left[\dfrac{{h}^{3}}{16} - \dfrac{{h}^{3}}{24}\right] = \dfrac{Lρg{h}^{3}}{16 \times 6}$

So, $\dfrac{{τ}_{1}}{{τ}_{2}} = 16$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Air (density $ρ$ ) is being blown on a soap film (surface tension $T$ ) by a pipe of radius& $R$ with its opening right next to the film. The film is deformed and a bubble detaches from the film when the shape of the deformed surface is a hemisphere. Given that the dynamic pressure on the film due to the air blown at speed $v$ is $\dfrac{1}{2}ρv^{2},$& the speed at which the bubble formed is
questions.solution:
Bubble detached from the look at ends of circumference, when force of dynamic pressure exceeds force of surface tension.

$⇒ {p}_{dynamic} \times$ Area ≥ Force of surface tension

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}ρv^{2} \times \piR^{2} \ge 2 \left(2\piRT\right)$

Note- that factor $2$ on right hand side appears as there are two sides of film surface.

$⇒ v \ge \sqrt{\dfrac{8T}{ρR}}$

$⇒ {v}_\min = \sqrt{\dfrac{8T}{ρR}}$
